BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.
- Employee bonuses: DD-005 AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- Ironquay IP: broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
- Export/privacy incident (DD-006): preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000): assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override.
- Title: require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.

IMPORTANT (playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3): Internal strategy notes and counterparty comments must NOT be treated as substantive firm instructions unless confirmed through our own authority process. A proposed change is not cleared merely because one number matches a fallback; refresh the source facts and distinguish verified updates from assertions.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel — Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status of Seller material:** Counterparty draft — reviewed against our playbook, not adopted. Note the Seller's own Disclosure Letter para 11 confirms nothing is "agreed" or approved; the "key negotiated positions" label in the cover note is Seller characterisation only.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap (cl 12.1)
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
- **Buyer wants:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- **Recommendation:** REJECT; counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- **Reason:** 20% matches our fallback number, but the fallback is unusable without Amelia Frost's written authority identifying this draft — none has been given, so the coincidence does not clear it.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket (cl 12.2)
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only recovery (deductible).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; first-dollar recovery once basket exceeded (tipping).
- **Recommendation:** REJECT; counter at playbook thresholds with tipping basket.
- **Reason:** Seller's thresholds are 5x ours and convert the basket into a deductible, materially eroding recovery on a AUD 24m deal.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit (cl 12.3 / 13)
- **Seller:** 18 months; plus a sweep that any limitation "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise".
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months; limitation applies only to General Warranty Claims.
- **Recommendation:** REJECT; counter at 24 months and delete the "all Claims" default.
- **Reason:** 18 months is an unauthorised fallback (no Frost approval), and the "all Claims" default is a back-door override of Fundamental/Tax/IP/indemnity regimes.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties folded into the general cap and time limits "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** Separate regime — 100% of price cap, minimum 6 years, outside de minimis/basket/knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** REJECT outright.
- **Reason:** "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cap title to what we are paying AUD 24m for at 20% and 18 months.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" — no fraud carve-out appears anywhere.
- **Buyer wants:** Express carve-out of fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance, to maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation:** REJECT; insert carve-out as a non-negotiable.
- **Reason:** Playbook says no one may waive this; a limitation purporting to cover fraud is also of doubtful enforceability and signals a drafting problem across cl 9.3/12.8/20.5.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope (Sch 7 / Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2)
- **Seller:** General disclosure of entire data room (DD-002–DD-012 as at 22 Sept 2026), Accounts, statutory registers and public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Specific, fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** REJECT paras 1.1–1.2; require specific disclosures against specific warranties with a fair-disclosure standard.
- **Reason:** General disclosure would make the warranties largely illusory, especially combined with the knowledge bar in cl 8.3.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier (cl 8.3)
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Delete blanket exclusion; any qualifier limited to named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry; never applies to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** REJECT and delete; if any qualifier survives, it must be on the Seller side only.
- **Reason:** "Discoverable" plus "advisers" is a constructive-knowledge bar that, with general disclosure, would neutralise the warranty package entirely.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3)
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours; consent deemed satisfied on delivery of counterparty's written consent. Disclosure Letter para 2 confirms **no** final consent and **no** evidence cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- **Buyer wants:** Condition precedent requiring effective consent **and** evidence that cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery.
- **Recommendation:** REJECT; redraft CP accordingly. The cover-note phrase "is addressed" is contradicted by the Seller's own disclosure.
- **Reason:** Bluefen is ~30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m) — reasonable endeavours is insufficient for a consent of this materiality.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7)
- **Seller:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion". Disclosure para 3: not repaid, no discharge included.
- **Buyer wants:** Current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases delivered at Completion; any post-completion release needs an irrevocable bank undertaking + Frost approval.
- **Recommendation:** REJECT; require payout letter and deed of release as Completion deliverables.
- **Reason:** Buying debt-free/cash-free with AUD 3.2m of secured debt and no release at Completion is incompatible with the price basis.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses (DD-005 / funds flow)
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 "a matter for the Seller", not itemised in funds flow. Disclosure para 5 confirms omission and is silent on payroll tax/super/on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs as a specific line item or expressly Seller-funded; funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Recommendation:** REJECT; add line item (bonuses + quantified on-costs) and treat as Debt/transaction cost reducing price or Seller-paid at Completion.
- **Reason:** A silent omission means the Company (post-Completion, i.e. Buyer) bears a known AUD 420k+ liability triggered by the deal itself.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity (cl 11.1)
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate". DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in data room.
- **Buyer wants:** Broadened indemnity (title defects, third-party claims, re-procurement costs) while preserving the cl 7.3 cure mechanism; independent verification of the AUD 180k position.
- **Recommendation:** REJECT narrow indemnity; counter with broadened indemnity + Completion deliverable of payment receipt and confirmatory IP assignment.
- **Reason:** Until every SOW3 fee is cleared, the Project Materials have not transferred under cl 7.3 — this is a title-to-IP issue, not just a payment issue, and the AUD 180k is unverified either way.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006 / cl 4.6 / Sch 6)
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material; ~1,240 records, no confirmed breach, no loss amount.
- **Buyer wants:** Log preservation, completed investigation, periodic updates pre-Completion, and a specific indemnity for costs/liabilities flowing from the incident — without assuming a breach, harm, notification duty or any number in either direction.
- **Recommendation:** DO NOT ACCEPT "not material" characterisation; require investigation covenant + specific indemnity; keep assessment open.
- **Reason:** Neither side has facts to call it material or immaterial yet; a specific indemnity allocates the unknown to the party that controlled the system.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011)
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000) are ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Buyer wants:** Assessment of timing, terminability, accrual and necessity before classification; no automatic Debt treatment or price deduction.
- **Recommendation:** HOLD — request renewal terms and timing; reserve position pending DD.
- **Reason:** The Seller's own disclosure para 8 says it does not state whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course, so "ordinary course" is assertion, not fact.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Cl 12.3/13 ("all Claims unless expressly stated"), cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 ("all Claims of any nature"), Fundamental folded into general, Tax/IP "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, payment/leakage and covenant claims each with their own cap, period and thresholds; no hidden general-regime override.
- **Recommendation:** REJECT all four override mechanisms; insert an express priority clause that general limitations apply only to General Warranty Claims.
- **Reason:** The draft collapses every category into the weakest regime via multiple separate clauses — fixing one leaves the others operative.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by Company share register at DD-012. Disclosure para 10 concedes this is the source relied on, not Buyer verification.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence — ASIC searches, PPSR, Riverlark/other security releases, board and shareholder authorisations, executed transfers, no-encumbrance confirmations.
- **Recommendation:** NOT SUFFICIENT; obtain independent verification before signing and again at Completion.
- **Reason:** DD-012 is a Seller-supplied internal register and, with AUD 3.2m of secured Riverlark debt outstanding, encumbrance over the shares cannot be ruled out from it.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** "Settled under the general regime above" (20% cap / 18 months / AUD 25k–250k thresholds).
- **Buyer wants:** Terms remain OPEN; separate Tax and IP regimes to be negotiated; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
- **Recommendation:** REJECT the "settled" characterisation in writing; record Tax/IP as open items on the issues list.
- **Reason:** Nothing has been agreed through our authority process, and silence risks the Seller later asserting acquiescence to the general regime.

---

### Overall
The draft is not "fair and balanced": it combines a below-authority cap and period, deductible thresholds, general disclosure, a constructive-knowledge bar, no fraud carve-out, and four separate mechanisms sweeping every claim category into the general regime — while the Seller's own Disclosure Letter confirms the Bluefen consent, Riverlark release, Ironquay assignment and bonus funding are all unresolved. **Recommend a full mark-up to playbook positions on all 16 items, with SPA-N-001/003 held at starting positions absent Frost written authority, and SPA-N-013/016 formally reserved as open.**
